paragraphs: Rabbi Marinus, son of Rabbi Hoshaya the Great.

He is mentioned in the Jerusalem Talmud, Gittin ch. 4, halakhah 6, disagreeing there with his father; and in Bereshit Rabbah 91:9: Rabbi Hanina and Rabbi Marinus, both of them in the name of Abba Nehorai; and he is mentioned in Shir HaShirim Rabbah 4:12, where it reads Rabbi Marinot (Hyman proposes Marinus) son of Rabbi Hoshaya.
And we find Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Marinus in Eichah Rabbah, end of ch. 2.
Hyman criticizes Seder HaDorot for making three entries out of him and conflating the Tanna and Amora; he maintains that there are only two.

notes.text: Hyman criticizes three entries while distinguishing a Tanna and an Amora. The local edition preserves that argument without merging authorities.

In the consulted Gittin 4:6 Hoshaya permits and his son Marinus forbids; Zeira and Yose then reconcile the positions by different circumstances. Hyman’s statement that he disagrees with his father is retained without suppressing that surrounding reconciliation.
